title: Matt Damon Called Mumbai the First Real Audience for The Odyssey. Then He Named the Indian Director He’s Owed a Film for Twenty Years.
excerpt: Christopher Nolan’s epic had its first public screening at PVR IMAX Phoenix Palladium — and between the standing ovations, Damon revealed he almost starred in Shekhar Kapur’s The Four Feathers before Bourne got in the way.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Mumbai hosted the global premiere of Christopher Nolan's film, The Odyssey.
  • Matt Damon expressed gratitude for Indian audiences, calling them the first real viewers of the film.
  • Damon revealed he owes Indian director Shekhar Kapur a collaboration from 20 years ago.
  • The Odyssey received an A-certificate in India with zero cuts, contrasting with Oppenheimer's release.
  • The film releases in Indian theatres on July 17, featuring a star-studded cast.
Mumbai's Premiere Significance
›Mumbai was one of four cities for The Odyssey's premiere.
›Nolan has filmed in India for two previous projects.
›The film is shot entirely on IMAX cameras.
›Damon called Indian audiences enthusiastic and knowledgeable.
There's a reason Christopher Nolan chose Mumbai. Not as an afterthought, not as a late addition to the press tour. Mumbai — alongside London, Paris, and New York — was one of four cities handpicked for the global premiere of **The Odyssey**, Nolan's adaptation of Homer's ancient Greek epic and the first feature film ever shot entirely on IMAX cameras. The screening took place Friday evening at PVR ICON IMAX, Phoenix Palladium in Lower Parel, and what unfolded inside that theatre was the kind of moment India's film culture has been building toward for decades. ![Christopher Nolan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/49/ChrisNolanBFI150224_%2810_of_12%29_%2853532289710%29_%28cropped2%29.jpg) Nolan, producer **Emma Thomas**, and lead actors **Matt Damon** and **Tom Holland** arrived in Mumbai on Friday morning, checking into the Taj Mahal Palace before heading to the premiere. When the lights came up after nearly three hours of ocean storms, ancient gods, and what early reviews are calling Damon's finest performance, the director stepped onto the stage. > "You are amongst the first audiences in the world to see this film. Indian audiences are some of the most enthusiastic and knowledgeable cinematic audiences in the world. For many years, I've wanted to come here and launch one of our films." — Christopher Nolan > **"For many years, I've wanted to come here and launch one of our films." — Christopher Nolan He wasn't being diplomatic."** He wasn't being diplomatic. Nolan has filmed in India twice — at Mehrangarh Fort in Jodhpur for *The Dark Knight Rises* and in Mumbai for *Tenet*, where he cast **Dimple Kapadia** in a pivotal role. India isn't new territory for him. What's new is the respect of a premiere. Then it was Damon's turn. The actor who plays **Odysseus** — a warrior trying to get home — got visibly emotional. > "This is the first real audience we've been in front of that has seen the film. It means the world to us that you liked it. We worked very, very hard on this film. It's the result of thousands of people pushing themselves so that you can see it this way." — Matt Damon ![Matt Damon — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/MattDamon-byPhilipRomano.jpg/3840px-MattDamon-byPhilipRomano.jpg) And then came the confession nobody expected. During the press conference, Damon revealed that he was originally attached to star in **Shekhar Kapur's** *The Four Feathers* — the 2002 historical war drama that eventually went to the late **Heath Ledger**. Damon had to pull out because of scheduling conflicts with *The Bourne Identity*. > "The filmmaker that everyone wanted to collaborate with was Shekhar Kapur. I was really upset when I couldn't do The Four Feathers because I was signed up for a Bourne movie. He's always been on my list. That's like a twenty-year-old little debt I've been carrying around in my pocket." — Matt Damon
The Odyssey's Certification
›The film received an A-certificate in India.
›It has a runtime of 2 hours and 52 minutes.
›The film was approved with zero cuts.
›This contrasts with the controversy of Oppenheimer's release.
For the diaspora audience watching from living rooms in New Jersey, Toronto, and London, this is the kind of validation that doesn't come with box office numbers. Hollywood's most bankable A-lister, in India, publicly naming the man who gave us *Bandit Queen*, *Mr. India*, and *Elizabeth* as someone he's owed a collaboration for two decades. ![Shekhar Kapur — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a5/Shri_Shekhar_Kapur.jpg) **Tom Holland**, whose Spider-Man films have made him one of the biggest draws in Indian multiplexes, closed the evening with characteristic grace: > "No one brings energy to a movie theatre like you do here in India. Thank you for supporting us. I cannot wait to be back." — Tom Holland The Odyssey has already cleared India's Central Board of Film Certification with **zero cuts** — a pointed contrast to the controversy that surrounded *Oppenheimer* during its 2023 release. The film carries an A-certificate with a runtime of two hours and fifty-two minutes. For NRIs and diaspora cinephiles, the practical takeaway: this is an IMAX film in the truest sense. Nolan shot every frame on IMAX cameras. If there was ever a reason to find the biggest screen near you — whether that's in Mumbai, Manhattan, or Mississauga — this is it. The film releases in Indian theatres on **July 17**, with the cast including **Zendaya** as Athena, **Anne Hathaway** as Penelope, **Robert Pattinson** as Antinous, **Charlize Theron**, and **Lupita Nyong'o**. Emma Thomas, Nolan's wife and producing partner, put the India premiere in context: "The future is in theatres," she said. Looking at the crowd that had packed Lower Parel on a Friday night to watch a Greek epic filmed on IMAX, it was hard to argue. Twenty years ago, Matt Damon missed his chance to work with an Indian filmmaker. He hasn't forgotten. Neither should Shekhar Kapur.
